MEMORANDUM FOR : JAPANESE GOVERNMENT.
SUBJECT : Dissolution or Liquidation of Major Financial or Industrial Enterprises.
1. Reference Memorandum for the Japanese Government from General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, AG 091.3 (20 Oct 45) ESS, SCAPIN 162, 20 October 1945, subject: Dissolution or Liquidation of Major Financial or Industrial Enterprises.
2. Paragraph 1 of Memorandum for the Japanese Government, dated 20 October 1945, reference 1, above, is hereby amended to read as follows:
“1. No approval will be given to plans or proposals submitted to you for the dissolution or liquidation of any holding company or ‘Zaibatsu Concern’ without prior submission to this headquarters.”
FOR THE SUPREME COMMANDER:
R.M. LEVY
Colonel, AGD
Adjutant General

MEMO FOR RECORD : (SCAPIN - 162/1)
ECW/RMG/jm
2 September 1949
1. References are:
a. AG 091.3 (20 Oct 45) ESS, SCAPIN 162, 20 October 1945, subject: Dissolution or Liquidation of Major Financial or Industrial Enterprises.
b. AG 091.3 (20 Oct 45) ESS, SCAPIN 162/1, subject: Dissolution or Liquidation of Major Financial or Industrial Enterprises.
2. Implementation of SCAPIN 162 reference 1a above, was effected by the Japanese Government in Article 1 of Imperial Ordinance No. 657 of 1945. That article required companies with capital in excess of \5 million (major industrial concerns), as well as holding companies and restricted concerns, to obtain prior approval of the Japanese Government for dissolution or liquidation.
3. In light of the progress in completion of financial reorganizations of major industrial concerns under the Enterprise Reorganization and Reconstruction Law: Law No. 40 of 1946, and of the progress made generally by such concerns in their financial rehabilitation, continued surveillance for the dissolution and liquidation thereof by either SCAP or the Japanese Government is considered unnecessary. Such actions will, with the amendment of SCAPIN 162, as effected by SCAPIN 162/1, reference 1b, above, and the appropriate amendment of Ordinance No. 657, be subject to the provisions of the Commercial Code of Japan. This limits the continued surveillance for this purpose to "holding companies and Zaibatsu concerns."
4. This action is in consonance with the SCAP policy of removing controls as quickly as circumstances permit.
5. Concurrence: ESS/JF
